title: Frozen validation protocol
description: One record per validation protocol: the decision taken BEFORE a study ran, including the tolerance that decides its outcome. A study manifest under validation/cross-implementation/studies/ points at one of these through protocolRef and carries the record's digest, so a tolerance loosened after a result appears stops matching and the diff says 'the frozen protocol changed' rather than 'one number moved'. Validated by scripts/verify-cross-implementation-study.mjs. Writing a protocol moves no claim's evidence level; promotion is a separate, human act recorded in docs/validation/claim-register.yaml.

protocolId.description: Stable identity, and the file's basename before .protocol.json. An example protocol must be prefixed EXAMPLE- and carry example: true.

example.description: True only for a template protocol, which may only be referenced by an example manifest.

question.description: What the study is trying to find out, in one sentence, written before it ran.

recordWrittenOn.description: The date this file was written. Freeze provenance is per claim, not per record: see claims[].freeze. A record-level frozen date used to live here and it was wrong, because one protocol can govern claims whose tolerances were fixed at different times and under different conditions.

claims.description: One entry per claim this protocol governs. A study manifest's claimId must appear here, and its metrics must equal the entry's metrics exactly.

decisionRule.description: What outcome follows from what measurement, decided in advance. Written so that a reader can apply it to the numbers without consulting the author.

digest.description: sha256 over the canonical form of every field of this record except this one. The verifier recomputes it, and a study manifest repeats it in protocolRef.digest.

datasetIds.description: The registered datasets this protocol admits for the claim. A study manifest may not use a dataset outside this list.

parameterSetIds.description: The parameter sets this protocol admits for the claim. A study manifest may not use a parameter set outside this list.

toleranceDerivation.description: Where the tolerance came from. 'It is what the comparison happened to reach' is not a derivation.

freeze.description: When this claim's tolerance was fixed, and whether that was before its result existed. Per claim, because one protocol can govern claims whose tolerances were fixed at different times: in this repository slope and hillshade were preregistered three weeks before their references were generated, and aspect was not.

status.description: preregistered: the tolerance was on record while this claim had no result, so the result could not have chosen it. adopted-with-result: the tolerance was fixed in the same change that produced the result. The second is not necessarily wrong - a tolerance carried over from a sibling claim can be perfectly defensible - but it is a weaker thing and it may not be described as the first.

on.description: The date the tolerance was fixed, as the witness commit shows it.

witnessCommit.description: The commit a reader checks. For preregistered, the earliest commit that shows this tolerance while the claim had no result; a later commit that also shows it proves less. Required as a hash and not as prose so that checking it is a git command, not an interpretation.

witness.description: What that commit contains, in enough detail to look up. A promise that the freeze happened is not a witness.

resultLandedOn.description: The date this claim's result first existed. Required by rule R11 before any manifest asserting a measured outcome may cite this protocol, so the freeze cannot be left unfalsifiable by omitting the other half of the comparison.

resultCommit.description: The commit that landed the result.

atInstant.description: ISO instant of the freeze commit. Present when the freeze and its result fall on the same day, so the ordering is decidable from the record alone. CI clones shallow and a squashed witness is unreachable from the default branch, so a check that needs history to answer this cannot answer it where it runs.

resultAtInstant.description: ISO instant of the result commit, paired with atInstant. P10 compares both against their commits wherever the history is available.

metrics.description: The agreement gate. Same shape as a study manifest's metrics block, and a manifest that points here must match it field for field.
